glm_5/001: The strategy for this policy is to use a Minimax search with Alpha-Beta pruning to determine the best move. The evaluation function focuses on minimizing the number of connected components of the current player's pieces (connectivity is the win condition) while maximizing the opponent's fragmentation. The search explores the game tree to a fixed depth to find the move that leads to the most favorable board state.
glm_5/002: The strategy for this policy is based on an Iterative Deepening Minimax search with Alpha-Beta pruning. The core heuristic focuses on minimizing the number of connected components for the current player while maximizing the opponent's components, as the victory condition is to connect all pieces. The search is optimized by pre-calculating line piece counts to speed up move generation and using a simple mobility/centralization heuristic for tie-breaking. The policy strictly adheres to the time limit by tracking execution time and returning the best move found from the deepest completed search depth.

The move generation strictly follows the Lines of Action rules regarding movement distance and blocking. Move ordering is applied to prioritize captures, which helps improve the efficiency of the alpha-beta pruning.

glm_5/005: The strategy for this policy is based on a Minimax search with Alpha-Beta pruning to look ahead several moves. The evaluation function prioritizes the primary win condition: connecting all friendly pieces into a single contiguous group. To guide the search in intermediate states, it uses a heuristic that minimizes the number of disconnected groups (components) and encourages pieces to move closer together (using pairwise Manhattan distances). The search depth is adapted based on the number of pieces on the board to ensure the move is computed within the time limit.
